note: Real 2026 election results. Election night is the preliminary count as reported by the media on the night. Official is the Electoral Commission's final result, including special votes, declared 27 November 2026.

electionNight.counted: 90.6% of results counted, before special votes
electionNight.sourceNotes: Party vote shares for National, Labour, Greens, ACT, Opportunity and Te Pāti Māori are as reported at 90.6% counted. NZ First (9.85%) is the reported coalition total of 50.2% less National and ACT. With these shares, the game's seat calculator gives the reported Parliament of 129: National 41 electorates on an entitlement of 36, Te Pāti Māori 5 electorates on an entitlement of 1, the National, ACT and NZ First bloc on 66, Labour, Greens and Te Pāti Māori on 56, and Opportunity on 7. Labour and the Greens' 24 electorates are split 23 to 1 (Auckland Central); the exact split does not change any party's seats.
electionNight.marginalNote: Seats with leads of a few hundred votes on election night. Hold chances are a game estimate: special votes have usually moved results slightly to the left.

official.counted: all votes counted, including 484,865 special votes
official.sourceNotes: Official result declared by the Electoral Commission on 27 November 2026, as reported by 1News, The Spinoff and the Electoral Commission notice reproduced by whatsoninvers.nz. Party votes: Labour 863,238, National 819,012, Green 406,356, ACT 304,521, NZ First 277,565, Opportunity 175,093, Te Pāti Māori 18,310 of 2,888,890. Electorates: National 40, Labour 22, Green 3 (Auckland Central, Wellington Bays, Wellington North), ACT 1 (Epsom), Te Pāti Māori 5. Changed from election night: Hamilton East and Wairarapa to Labour, Wellington Bays to the Greens. Judicial recount applications close 2 December 2026.
official.summaryNote: Since election night, special votes moved Hamilton East and Wairarapa from National to Labour and Wellington Bays from Labour to the Greens: National is down to 40 seats and the Greens up to 17. National, ACT and NZ First have 65, one short of a majority, so neither side can govern without Opportunity. Recount applications close on 2 December.
